newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips weaken, but SAX firms 0.14 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips weaken, but SAX firms 0.14 pts.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mostly down in flat trading on Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with a slight increase in Slovnaft helping to push the SAX index up 0.14 points to 212.70.
Brokers said the leading issues on the BSE have been generally suffering from the current downward trend on the Slovak capital market.
"It seems the time has come for a correction of the bullish trend, which was affecting our market since the beginning of this year," Libor Chrast of ING Barings said.
The most heavily-weighted issue on the index, oil refinery Slovnaft, dominated trading on the bourse floor, as it 22,561 shares traded and the issued closed one crown higher at 951 crowns.
"Slovnaft was boosted only by a single block-deal of some more than 22,000 shares at 950 crowns," Chrast said. "However, I consider its current price as the real and stabilised."
He said other blue chips traded significantly small volumes, as he did not expect improvement in the near future.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta traded 15 shares, closing down 50 crowns at 2,050. Commercial bank VUB closed down 20 crowns at 1,875, with 28 traded shares.

Overall volume fell to 103,362 shares, from 945,865 shares traded on Friday, while turnover decreased to 107.73 million crowns, from 502.3 million. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687
